extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants (principal investigators) and institutional officials considering rebuttal or appeal of peer review
extracted.subtask_short: NIH peer review rebuttal and appeal
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and guidance for NIH applicants on submitting rebuttals after summary statements and formal appeals of National Advisory Council decisions, including who to send them to, required signatures and documentation, scope of review, timing, and likely outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of rebuttal
rubrics_metrics.description: A rebuttal is available after the applicant has received the summary statement that documents the results of the initial review of the application's scientific and/or technical merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NIH provides an applicant who feels some aspect of handling or peer review was inappropriate, biased, or wrong with the opportunity to submit a detailed letter rebutting the review after receipt of the summary statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebuttal submission recipient
rubrics_metrics.description: Rebuttals should be submitted to the Program Administrator of the relevant NIH Institute/Center (IC) responsible for the application, not to the Scientific Review Administrator of the initial review group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit the detailed letter rebutting the review to the IC Program Administrator; do not send it to the Scientific Review Administrator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebuttal vs additional information determination
rubrics_metrics.description: The IC will judge whether the letter is a rebuttal or simply a communication providing additional information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If judged to be a rebuttal and not simply additional information, it will usually be made available to the IC's National Advisory Council/Board for consideration if IC staff cannot handle the concerns administratively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council action on rebuttal
rubrics_metrics.description: If the National Advisory Council finds the applicant's objections have merit, it may recommend that the application be deferred and rereviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Council concurs with the initial review and deems it should stand, the applicant may submit a formal appeal of the Council's decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal appeal joint signature requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The PI and the applicant institution, represented by the institutional official authorized to sign applications, must jointly sign an appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The institutional official's signature indicates that the applicant institution endorses both the form and substance of the appeal (ref: NIH Manual Chapter 4518).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal content and documentation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The appeal letter must explain fully the reasons for the disagreement and append supporting documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The joint-signed appeal must be sent to the NIH Peer Review Appeals Officer (address provided). Include complete explanation and supporting documents to substantiate procedural flaws alleged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal submission address / officer
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal appeals must be sent to the NIH Appeals Officer at the Office of the Director, National Institutes of Health (address included).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mail to: NIH Appeals Officer, Office of the Director, National Institutes of Health, 6701 Rockledge Drive, Room 6192, Bethesda, MD 20892.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of appeals (what is reviewed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals examine only whether there were any flaws in the peer review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The most favorable possible outcome from an appeal is a decision that the application be rereviewed; appeals do not reassess the scientific merits except insofar as procedural flaws affected review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possible appeal outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Either (a) the application is found to have been substantially flawed in peer review and is rereviewed, or (b) the review is found not substantially flawed and stands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If minor flaws did not affect the recommendation, the review would stand and the application would not be rereviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of the appeal process
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeal cases involve several steps and may take at least four months (or one review cycle) to complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of the time required, applicants should consider timing when deciding whether to appeal versus revising and resubmitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration whether to appeal vs revise/resubmit
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should weigh whether deficiencies in the review were substantive enough to have had a major deleterious effect on the application's review before pursuing an appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given limited favorable outcomes and the time required for appeals, if deficiencies were not substantive, applicants may wish to revise and resubmit instead of appealing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-review receipt and assignment concerns handled separately
rubrics_metrics.description: Concerns about acceptance for review, responsiveness to an RFA, other receipt issues, or referral, when submitted prior to the initial review, are the responsibility of the Division of Research Grants (DRG) or of the assigned IC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The DRG or IC process provides two internal opportunities (both internal to DRG or IC) for applicant concerns to be addressed prior to initial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding decisions are not appealable
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions regarding the funding of applications may not be appealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals examine only peer review process flaws; funding actions are external to peer review and are outside the appeals process.
